newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - SKF Q1 profit seen 25 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - SKF Q1 profit seen 25 pct lower.

text.p: Swedish ball bearing manufacturer SKF is expected on Tuesday to show a 25 percent fall in first quarter profit after financial items to 651 million crowns, a Reuters poll of 16 analysts found.
Forecasts ranged from 550 million crowns to 829 million crowns. In the first quarter of 1996, the company's profit was 811 million crowns.
Analysts said there was uncertainty regarding sales volumes and product prices.
"SKF has said that it doesn't expect price increases this year," an analyst said.
"European sales volumes development are of key importance, but I don't think the development is good at the beginning of the year. The last two quarters will, however, show an upturn."
"The first quarter in 1996 was a positive surprise and I think analysts have underestimated the market this time too," an analyst said. "Car sales have, for example, been strong."
For the full year, the profit is expected to increase to 2.71 billion crowns from 2.41 billion crowns in 1996.
Analysts forecast a 1998 profit of 3.26 billion crowns, which is four percent lower than forecasts made before the company's 1996 annual report was released in February.
SKF will change accounting practices to show operating profit rather than profit after financial items for its divisions.

Sources for the poll were from Aros, Carnegie, Den Danske Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Enskilda, Erik Penser FK, FIBA Nordic, Fischer Partners, Foreningsbanken, Goldman Sachs, Matteus, Merrill Lynch, Myrberg & Wiklund, Paribas, Swedbank, and Ohman.
